text:
maria: FYI - we started seeing GPU hosts in eu-west intermittently fail to bring up the nvidia kernel module after yesterday's kernel-6.x image rollout. ~20% of the pool flapped between 02:00-04:00 UTC. Repro is pretty consistent on the new image.

kevin: Can you paste the dmesg / error? Is it a taint or undefined symbol?

maria: dmesg snippets: 
`[    6.123456] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel`
`[    6.123789] nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout`
`[    6.124001] nvidia: probe of nvidia0 failed with error -22`

sam: Jobs in the affected nodes fail to initialise NCCL. Example from task logs: `NCCL WARN Call to cuDevicePrimaryCtxGetState failed : unknown error` then `failed to allocate memory for NV device`. A few containers crashed during cuInit().

carol: Were DKMS hooks supposed to rebuild the driver against the new kernel? Did cloud-init run successfully?

maria: DKMS shows failures in cloud-init log: `dkms build nvidia/525.89.02 for 6.1.0-rc headers: failed (no such file or directory)` — looks like host image doesn't include matching kernel-headers for the released kernel variant. Also noticed our image builder used gcc-12 whereas runtime expects gcc-11 for that module ABI.

dave: Sounds like a header mismatch + ABI toolchain issue. Kernel 6.x changed some internal layout and our prebuilt driver blob (525.* closed) wasn't compiled against that exact header set. Two paths: (1) ensure headers + same gcc are installed and let DKMS rebuild; (2) revert nodes to 5.15 host kernel while we prepare a rebuilt driver or use a compatible OSS driver.

infra-bot: [alert] autoscaler drained 12 nodes in eu-west/gpu-pool-2 due to repeated module failures. Rolling fallback to higher-cost on-demand instances in us-east started.

kevin: We should canary rollback to the previous kernel image for the rest of eu-west. Also need a quick health-check script to detect `disagrees about version of symbol module_layout` in dmesg and mark node unschedulable before jobs start. That will prevent repeated pod crash churn.

maria: Agreed. Plan: 1) Pin the eu-west pool to kernel-5.15 image and redeploy today (kevin). 2) I will start a DKMS + builder job to produce a driver build against kernel-6.1 headers and gcc-12 (sam + maria). 3) dave will help validate driver ABI on a canary VM.

sam: Short term thermal: enable node taint `gpu:drivers-failed` on affected hosts so schedulers skip them. We'll reroute capacity to unaffected pools. Also watch for NCCL timeouts across the cluster — may need to pause heavy multi-GPU jobs.

carol: FYI this caused quota bump in cloud billing because we spun up replacement on-demand GPUs in us-east as fallback — rough estimate $3.5k extra over 36 hours. We should include cost owner in postmortem.

maria: I'll open an incident ticket + postmortem draft. Initial RCA candidate: kernel image built without matching kernel headers in our artifact (stripped to save size), causing DKMS rebuild failures; plus prebuilt proprietary driver not compatible with 6.x ABI.

kevin: For the rollout process: add a gating step that verifies DKMS can build driver against the exact image artifacts (headers + toolchain) in a CI VM before pushing kernel upgrade to any GPU pool. Also add a canary window of 1h and an automated rollback if >5% of pool nodes show module load errors.

dave: I'll run a bisect job to identify the exact kernel change that breaks the prebuilt driver and post back a delta patch or workaround. ETA for canary validation 24-48h.

maria: Action items:
- kevin: start pinned rollback for eu-west (ETA 2h)
- sam + maria: build & test DKMS-driven driver for 6.x (ETA 48h)
- dave: kernel bisect and validation (ETA 48h)
- carol: cost tracking for the incident (ongoing)

maria: tagging ops on-call @kevin for rollout. Will update thread with cloud-init logs and the list of affected AMIs. :white_check_mark:
